 Kazakhstan vs. Slovakia - Head-to-head record
 Kazakhstan and Slovakia have met three times, with the hosts holding a narrow advantage of two victories to one. None of their previous encounters have ended in a draw .
 Kazakhstan won both meetings during the 2022 UEFA Nations League, securing a 1-0 away victory in Trnava before following it up with a 2-1 home success.
 Slovakia gained some revenge in September 2026, winning 2-1 in the reverse fixture. All three meetings have been decided by a single goal, suggesting that Kazakhstan could provide another competitive challenge despite their difficult campaign.

 Kazakhstan - Hosts Fighting to Avoid Bottom Spot
 Kazakhstan enter their final Nations League fixture without a victory in the competition and facing the possibility of finishing bottom of Group C3. Let’s examine their recent performances and expected line-up.
 Recent form
 Kazakhstan have endured a disappointing Nations League campaign, recording two draws and three defeats from their opening five matches . John van ‘t Schip’s side suffered another setback on Friday, losing 2-1 away to Moldova after conceding the decisive goal in the 77th minute.
 That result extended their winless run across all competitions to seven matches, with their last victory coming against Comoros in March. Kazakhstan have scored and conceded in each of those seven fixtures, highlighting their defensive vulnerabilities despite showing some attacking consistency.
 Their hopes of finishing in the top two have already ended, but a victory over Slovakia could still give them a chance of avoiding last place. They would also need the Faroe Islands to lose against Moldova to remain in contention for third position.
 Van ‘t Schip could make changes after Friday’s defeat, with Sergey Maliy available again following a one-match suspension. He may replace Temirlan Erlanov in central defence, while Yan Vorogovskiy could start at left wing-back after replacing Nauryzbek Zhagorov at half-time against Moldova.

 Slovakia - Group Winners Looking to Finish Unbeaten
 Slovakia have already secured promotion to League B after an impressive Nations League campaign. With the top spot guaranteed, Vladimir Weiss’s side will be looking to maintain their unbeaten record in their final group fixture.
 Recent form
 Slovakia have collected 11 points from their opening five Nations League matches, recording three victories and two draws . Their performances have been particularly impressive against Moldova and Kazakhstan, with eight goals scored across those three wins.
 However, they have been unable to beat the Faroe Islands, drawing both meetings. Their most recent fixture ended 2-2 on Friday, when Slovakia came from behind to preserve their unbeaten record and extend their run without defeat across all competitions to eight matches.
 Despite those dropped points, Slovakia have secured first place in Group C3 with a four-point advantage over their nearest challengers. They have scored 11 goals and conceded four in the competition, although their only clean sheets have come against Moldova.
 Weiss is expected to rotate his squad with promotion already confirmed. Martin Valjent is suspended after accumulating yellow cards, potentially opening the door for Tobias Paliscak at right-back. Ivan Mesik, Matus Bero and Robert Bosenik are also candidates to start.

 Predictions for Kazakhstan vs. Slovakia - Visitors to continue strong run
 Slovakia arrive with an eight-match unbeaten run and have scored at least twice in seven of those fixtures. Their attacking consistency makes Slovakia to be winning at half-time an interesting option, particularly against a Kazakhstan side that has struggled defensively.
 Kazakhstan have conceded in each of their last seven matches, while Slovakia have scored 11 goals in five Nations League fixtures. These figures also support the possibility of over 0.5 goals in the first half, although the visitors could rotate their squad with promotion already secured.
 Despite Kazakhstan’s stronger historical head-to-head record, Slovakia have been the more consistent team throughout the campaign. Our main prediction is Slovakia to win , although the hosts’ need for points could make this a closer contest than the group standings suggest.
